results.note: 10,836 and 6,877 in Study Design; definitions in Demographic... 2nd paragraph; counts in Results and Table 3. 6,817 is the sum of the three groups (not printed); the percentages are of it, though the Results say 'full sample'.

Table 4/5 support-and-safety values match; intervals recomputed (-0.427 to -0.153; -0.855 to -0.385) and 3 x 0.62 = 1.86. Ratings are retrospective; the paper does not state the model type for the fear item.

The six covariates are the rows of Tables 4 and 5; the Analysis Framework paragraph says only that demographic and drinking-history covariates were included. Each model also held the motivation, ceremony and support variables.
2017-2019, English plus five languages, 10,836 and 6,877 in Study Design; church definition in Demographic... 2nd paragraph; counts in Results and Table 3. 6,817 is the groups' sum, not printed.
Table 3 values match. Years are means (SD 4.7, 3.1, 2.5); percentages are of those answering each item (residence N = 6,558; diagnoses N = 5,524).
Table 2 context-panel values match; 'offered' fits supports provided at the place of drinking (Methods). Results 2nd and 3rd paragraphs describe these differences.
Table 4/5 values match; the 10-50 Kessler range is stated in Mental Health, Wellbeing and Spirituality Variables, 1st paragraph; 3 x 0.62 = 1.86 recomputed.
Table 4/5 preparation values match; 3 x 0.25 = 0.75. The item wording comes from Table 1 (Additional supports), which the locator could add.
Covariates as in Tables 4-5. Times drunk: p < 0.001 for PWG, SF-12 MCS, K10 and PGIC. Diagnoses: SF-12 MCS -1.05, K10 0.73 (both p < 0.001); not PWG or PGIC.
